{{Quote|Would you look at that? A Twi'lek singing stone&hellip; all the way from Ryloth. What are the odds we'd stumble on something like that here, now?|Vette|audio=Vette-SingingStone.flac|<ref name="Date Night" />}}
'''Singing Stones''' were [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] that the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] people held sacred. The Twi'lek diaspora felt a strong spiritual connection to their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] through the stones, which also originated from Ryloth and, according to Twi'lek legend, were intoned to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy's]] vibrations and possessed mystical navigational powers. The Twi'lek maverick [[Vette]] was eager for one such stone on the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Makeb]].

==Description==
Singing Stones could appear as a rugged [[Color/Legends|maroon]] [[Gemstone/Legends|gemstone]]<ref name="Crafting" /> or as a spherical blue [[Crystal/Legends|crystal]].<ref name="Date Night" /> According to the mythology of the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] people of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]], where Singing Stones originated, the stones were in tune with the vibrations of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] and held mystical powers of navigation.<ref name="Codex" />

==History==
{{Quote|Sure would be a shame if this thing went for a little trip, back to the people it belongs to&hellip;|Vette|<ref name="Date Night" />}}
Most Singing Stones became lost as Ryloth experienced a tumultuous history of invasion, occupation, and civil war. By the [[Time/Legends|time]] of the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy-wide]] [[Sith Wars/Legends|struggle]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|reconstituted Sith Empire]], Singing Stones had become especially revered by the Twi'lek diaspora for providing a deep, spiritual connection to their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and cultural heritage.<ref name="Codex" />

Around [[3623 BBY]],<ref name="Date">{{TOR_updates|7.5.1}} 7.5.1: The Greatest Bounty, released in [[2024]], take place around [[3623 BBY]].</ref> during the [[Third Galactic War]] between the Republic and the Sith Empire, the Twi'lek maverick [[Vette]] found a Twi'lek singing stone on display at a [[Museum/Legends|museum]] in [[Talaos City]] on the planet [[Makeb]] and felt compelled to return it to her people.

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: The Old Republic: Legacy of the Sith}}
Tagging alongside the [[Alliance Commander|Commander]] of the [[Eternal Alliance]], Vette [[Slicer/Legends|sliced]] into the stone's display case and accidentally triggered the museum's security alarm. They nevertheless absconded with the stone after fending off [[Security droid/Legends|security droids]] and a crushing ceiling together.<ref name="Date Night" />
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Singing_Stone.png|thumb|right|4.1's Singing Stone]]
Singing Stones were introduced to the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity as a crafting material in Update 4.1 of the [[2011]] [[BioWare]] [[Star Wars video games|massively multiplayer online role-playing game]] ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'',<ref name="Crafting" /> which was launched as part of the [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Knights of the Fallen Empire|''Knights of the Fallen Empire'']] expansion in [[2016]].<ref name="4.1">{{TORweb|url=patchnotes/282016/game-update-4.1-anarchy-paradise-patch-notes|text=Game Update 4.1: Anarchy in Paradise Patch Notes}}</ref> [[Singing stone]]s first appeared in the new [[canon]] continuity's [[2015]] novel ''[[Dark Disciple]]'', written by [[Christie Golden]]. The novel adapts an unfinished eight-episode story arc for the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' television series, which was written by [[Katie Lucas]], [[Matt Michnovetz]], and [[Dave Filoni]].<ref name="DD">''[[Dark Disciple]]''</ref>

The singing stone in the canon continuity was first pictured as a blue stone named the [[Hayananeya]] in the [[Halcyon Legacy 1|first issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars: Halcyon Legacy]]'' [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]],<ref name="Halcyon 1">[[Halcyon Legacy 1|''Halcyon Legacy'' 1]]</ref> which was written by [[Ethan Sacks]], illustrated by [[Will Sliney]], and published by [[Marvel Comics]] on [[February 2]], [[2022]].<ref name="Marvel">{{Marvel|url=comics/issue/96844/star_wars_the_halcyon_legacy_2022_1|text=Star Wars: The Halcyon Legacy (2022) #1}}</ref> The Hayananeya singing stone was made as a physical prop for the [[Star Wars: Galactic Starcruiser|''Star Wars'': Galactic Starcruiser]] immersive hotel experience, which opened on [[March 1]] in the same year.<ref name="GS">[[Star Wars: Galactic Starcruiser|''Star Wars'': Galactic Starcruiser]]</ref> This appearance of the Twi'lek singing stone was subsequently introduced to the Legends continuity in the Date Night mission for Vette in ''The Old Republic''{{'s}} Update 7.5.1,<ref name="Date Night" /> launched as part of the game's [[Star Wars: The Old Republic: Legacy of the Sith|''Legacy of the Sith'']] expansion in [[2024]]. The Date Night mission is only available to [[Gender/Legends|male]] [[Empire's Wrath|Sith Warrior]] characters who have an active romance with Vette following ''Knights of the Fallen Empire''.<ref name="Romance">{{TORweb|url=info/news/article/20240820-0|text=Game Update 7.5.1 "The Greatest Bounty" is now live!}}</ref>
